source_verification.verified_title: Thermal Property Prediction of Eicosane-Fatty Acid Eutectic Phase Change Materials Using the Modified UNIFAC Model for Thermal Energy Storage Technology

aboutness.basis: Research object is low-temperature latent-heat storage materials and their thermophysical properties, not a geographical claim.
aboutness.verified_excerpt: Publisher abstract reports predicted and measured phase-change properties for eicosane mixed with lauric, myristic or palmitic acid; melting temperatures are approximately 31–34 °C. (Paraphrase.)

topic.label: Critical technology: Energy technologies
topic.basis: Experimental comparison of a thermodynamic materials-screening model is a substantive energy-storage research contribution, rather than a generic sustainability claim.

futures.mechanism: Computational screening and experimental validation of organic phase-change materials for low-temperature thermal storage.
futures.why_could_matter: If validated across additional mixtures and duty cycles, lower experimental screening costs could accelerate design of thermal buffers for building heating and cooling.
futures.uncertainty: Only publisher abstract examined. Long-term cycling, conductivity, integration cost, environmental performance and independent validation are unresolved.
futures.research_question: Under what operating conditions can model-selected organic eutectics outperform existing thermal-storage materials in European building systems?

eu_perspective.implications: EU research groups and thermal-storage manufacturers could evaluate whether the screening approach reduces material development costs for heat-pump and building thermal buffers.
eu_perspective.evidence_limits: Source reports laboratory-scale model validation, not European deployment, cost savings or competitiveness. EU connection is analyst interpretation; no independent replication established.

source_verification.verified_title: Knowledge Diplomacy and African Higher Education: Aid-Driven Research Co-operation in the Name of Economic Development

aboutness.basis: Publisher description specifies interview research involving university staff and students in Ethiopia, Tanzania, Mozambique and Malawi, with Swedish-supported research cooperation as a central object.
aboutness.verified_excerpt: Publisher description identifies bilateral research support and institutional change toward more research-intensive African universities. (Paraphrase.)

topic.label: Africa: Capacities for science and higher education
topic.basis: Direct examination of research capacity, doctoral training and international research cooperation in African higher education, including Sida programmes.

futures.mechanism: Research-capacity building through bilateral funding, doctoral education and African academic leadership.
futures.why_could_matter: The cases could inform European funders on designing durable and locally governed research partnerships rather than treating capacity as a simple function of foreign funding.
futures.uncertainty: Publisher description and contents establish scope but not detailed findings or causal effect sizes. Exact canonical DOI remains unconfirmed at the primary DOI record.
futures.research_question: Which features of bilateral research cooperation enable sustained research capacity and local agenda-setting in partner universities after external funding changes?

eu_perspective.implications: Swedish research cooperation with African universities is itself a European Member State partnership mechanism relevant to wider EU–Africa research-capacity and science-diplomacy programmes.
eu_perspective.evidence_limits: The Swedish cooperation is explicitly part of the book’s research object; application to EU-level programmes is analyst interpretation, not a demonstrated effect.

results.review_reason: Substantive regional priority and European partnership relevance are confirmed, but the exact canonical DOI could not be read from primary publisher DOI metadata.
